1) Traceability gaps: the narrative cites neighbor-comparison items (E22/E23/E24) but the top-level evidence_used list for the mechanism claim omits them, weakening auditability of the ICT-vs-TICT argument.
2) Major physics/consistency concern between computed excitation and observed emission: aTB reports excitation_energy 1.274 eV and s1_excitation_wavelength_nm ~973 nm (E61), while observed emission peaks are ~504–541 nm (E70–E72), implying ~2.3–2.5 eV. This mismatch is large enough that the aTB-derived “torsion/redistribution” cues may not correspond to the experimentally emissive state.
3) ESIPT is treated as “cannot be excluded,” but structure-based prerequisites appear absent: no tautomerizable proton-transfer motif and no HBD (compact_prior_metrics_v1 and structure_motif_profile summaries), which should materially downweight ESIPT relative to ICT/TICT given the allowed label set.

5) Emission-shift interpretation is underdetermined: the moderate blue shift from aggregate to solid/film (E72) can arise from multiple mechanisms (different aggregate types, exciton coupling, polarity/packing differences), not uniquely ICT vs TICT without spectral-shape/temperature/solvent dependence.
